fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Letter Swaps Across the Celtic Tongues", "body": "Dylan says he has spent the last month or two delving into the languages of Britain, Welsh, Cornish and Irish, along with Armorica in northwestern France, and argues they are all one language with the letters switched around. He reads the Irish mor, meaning great, against the Welsh mawr through the U, V and W interchange, ties it to the Phoenician, and follows it into the Italian mauro and Mauretania, the land of the great. Later he sets the Welsh name for Venus beside venery and the chase. Chance adds a point from Higgins: before printing, spelling was a free for all."}, {"title": "Occult Symbols as Inherited Tradition", "body": "Dylan traces his own entry point to arriving in Hollywood at 20 and being invited to parties full of powerful people, where he says he overheard a great deal as a fly on the wall. Having moved in those circles, and having met game developers on trips to E3, he concludes that the occult symbolism placed in films and games is simply their tradition, the way a Christian might hang a picture of Saint Luke without knowing its astrotheology. He insists the people running the system are not as sinister or as intimidating as many assume, and says real knowledge of this kind raises a person."}, {"title": "Gateways Through Debt and Doorstep Preachers", "body": "Chance names the Zeitgeist movie, seen as a senior in high school, as a first push, but faults it for presenting savior syncretism as a bullet list of fraud rather than as a reflection of nature. His real gateway, he says, was learning that money is debt, the subject of his English capstone project in college, and a holiday first viewing of the Die Hard trilogy, in which he noticed the villains steal only bearer bonds and gold, never debt notes. Gabe credits the Jehovah's Witnesses who cornered him as a child, saying the seed they planted about the Nephilim and ruling bloodlines still stands."}, {"title": "The Erotes and Their Musical Chairs", "body": "Gabe is studying the Erotes, the train of Aphrodite, and says there are seven of them but only six seats, so when someone wants to stir the ant farm the chairs get rearranged and nobody shares the same odd man out, which he links to the lockdowns. He reads one of them, Hedylogos or sweet talk, as a root of addiction and of hypnotic rhetoric carried by hand gestures. He notes the Erotes were once shown as grown youths and have been infantilized into babies over time. Chance shares Bellini's winged cherub heads, which Gabe agrees look placental."}, {"title": "Wrath as a Compliment in Disguise", "body": "When Chance reads a chat question calling the first Spirit Whirled book angry, Dylan pushes back hard, saying the research was done all at once and his audience voted to split it into several books. He concedes he wrote the first two or three books to his 16 year old self, the way he speaks, but rejects the label. Gabe answers through the Enneagram, calling wrath the shadow of the type one reformer and perfectionist, so a projection of wrath is a compliment in disguise. Dylan adds that he dislikes bearing false witness, saying the critic never met him and was not there when he wrote the book."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: It's the holiday season, so why not come and kick it with your favorite fiery syncromystics? Dylan Saccoccio and Gabe (Slick Dissident) will be with me tonight, taking your questions and calls.
